event_bins_authors: relative months n = -5..-1 and 1..6 (d_5..d_1, d1..d6); omitted: n = -6 and n = 0 (two normalizations, needed with treated-only samples); window -6..+6, no endpoint bins
event_omitted_period_authors: n = -6 and n = 0 (rel = -7 and -1 under the pipeline's g = first after month)
published_source: Shown only in Figure 4 of the published article; no printed value. Authors' code output recorded in authors_code_*. (papers/mnsc/mnsc.2023.01423.pdf, read Nov 4 2026: the figure plots the bin coefficients for months -5..-1 and +1..+6 with 90 percent confidence intervals, and no coefficient of this regression is printed in the main text, the notes or the online appendix; published_event_coefs is therefore null, and the authors' log bins are kept in authors_code_event_coefs.) Earlier: Replications/Main tables and figures/Figure4/Figure4log.log (authors' Stata log)
replication_status: exact (authors' code output: equal-weight mean of the post bins n = 1..6 -0.00753195, N 10470 (authors' log), reproduced by fixest to 5e-8 on the shipped data; shown only in Figure 4 (large investors, high-priced stocks) of the published article, no printed value to compare; verified against the article Nov 4 2026)
expected_twfe_source: fixest on the pipeline sample: y ~ i(relb, ref = -1) | stkcd + ym, relb = min(max(t - g, -7), 6), cluster stkcd (run_spec.R mapping with event_pre_min = -6, event_post_max = 5)
notes: Replications/Main tables and figures/Figure4/Figure4.do line 60: reghdfe largehold d_5 d_4 d_3 d_2 d_1 d1 d2 d3 d4 d5 d6 if dummyh==1 & <years>, absorb(stkcd month) cluster(stkcd month). fixest reproduces all 11 logged coefficients (max abs diff 4.7e-08); published_coef is the equal-weight average of d1..d6 (-0.007532), SE not in the log (fixest two-way SE of the average 0.012800). Window mapping: g = first after = 1 month, so n = rel + 1; event_pre_min = -6 and event_post_max = 5 reproduce the authors' leads (n = -5..-1) and post bins (n = 1..6) with reference n = 0. Deviation: run_spec.R estimates a single normalization (rel = -1) and bins endpoints (rel <= -7, rel >= 6), so it also estimates a coefficient for n = -6, which the authors omit, and the linear event-time component (not identified without never-treated units) is pinned down by the endpoint bins, mostly the later splits' post rows pooled in rel >= 6. Its TWFE post average on the pipeline sample is -0.008686 (expected SD units -0.012609); with the authors' two normalizations on the same pipeline sample it is -0.023804, and on the authors' sample -0.007532. The first-split coding drops 1118 of 10470 rows. Same sample as Table 8 col 5 (N 10,470). Event-window panel of split stocks only (A-share stocks with a split; rows are stock x event x month for months -6..+6 around each split, n = 0 is the split month, after = 1 for n = 1..6). Authors' regression pools all split events of a stock with stkcd FE (not stock x event FE), so a stock with several splits has after switching on and off across events and duplicate stkcd-month rows where event windows overlap. Pipeline coding (lead ruling): unit = stkcd, treat_var = after, treatment absorbing from the stock's FIRST split (g = first month with after = 1); run_spec.R drops later rows with after = 0 at t >= g (Hull fn. 6). Later events' after = 1 rows stay in as treated rows at long horizons of the first split. The few stkcd-month duplicates that survive the drop (overlapping windows) make the data a repeated cross-section in run_spec.R's test, so CSA takes the RC path (att_gt panel = FALSE) per PROTOCOL 5b(a). No never-treated stocks (identification from not-yet-split stocks), no always-treated stocks (every kept event has >= 4 pre-split rows). Cluster: authors use two-way stkcd and month clustering (reghdfe cluster(stkcd month)); run_spec.R supports one cluster variable, so cluster_var = stkcd (deviation, affects SEs only). time_var ym = year*12 + month - 1 (no interior calendar gaps). No article text or PDF in the project: published values are the authors' Stata log/outreg2 output shipped in the package; column numbers are outreg2 output order (not checked against the printed table). An open-access PDF URL is listed in data/frame/frame.csv for later verification.
pipeline_caveat: Treated-only sample: the TWFE event study's normalization differs from the authors' (single reference rel = -1 plus endpoint bins vs the authors' n = -6 and n = 0 omitted); run_spec TWFE post average -0.0087 vs -0.0238 under the authors' normalization on the same rows (raw units). CSA RC cells compare different stocks at t and g-1.
dup_collapse: Stray-duplicate ruling (PROTOCOL 5b, as mnsc.2023.4968), Nov 2: overlapping event windows repeat some stock-months; rows with the same (stkcd, ym, after, dummyh) have identical outcomes and are collapsed to one row with frequency weight w_mergedup (collapse_dups.R). TWFE and imputation point estimates are unchanged; CSA now uses the panel path.

event_structure.source: Replications/Main tables and figures/Figure4/Figure4.do line 60: tabulate n, gen(d) -> d_6..d6; reghdfe largehold d_5 d_4 d_3 d_2 d_1 d1-d6 if dummyh==.. & years, absorb(stkcd month) cluster(stkcd month): n = -6 and n = 0 omitted (two normalizations; treated-only sample). Rows are stock x split event x month, n = -6..6 around each split. Pipeline (lead ruling): treatment absorbing from the stock's first split, g = first-split month + 1 (adoption_var g_first_split), so rel = n - 1 on the first split's rows: n -5..-1 -> rel -6..-2, n 1..6 -> rel 0..5, omitted n -6, 0 -> rel -7, -1. Later splits' after = 1 rows fall at rel >= 6 and get their own open bin [6,null] (outside the authors' first-split window, not summarized); later splits' after = 0 rows at t >= g are dropped by the switch-off rule.
event_structure.verified: fixest with the authors' n dummies reproduces the 11 logged coefficients on their multi-event sample (max abs diff 4.68e-08, N 10470, two-way clustered). This structure on the pipeline sample (first-split coding, switch-off rows dropped, collapsed, N 9330) gives max abs diff 0.0283 vs the logged coefficients; post average -0.0236 vs -0.0075, pre average -0.0350 vs -0.0375 (raw). The gap is the design change (first-split coding), not the bins: on the first-split rows alone (rel >= 6 dropped) the structure equals the authors' n coding exactly but the sample loses the later splits.

adoption_var_note: First-split month + 1 per (stkcd, dummyh), built by ~/did_packages/_work/mnsc.2023.01423/adopt_dates.R (new file *_adopt.rds = the collapsed panel plus this column). treat_var gives the first OBSERVED after = 1 month, which is 1-3 months late for stocks whose n = 1 row is missing (T8/F4 high 3, F5 high 17, F5 non-high 22 stocks). No pre-sample adopters. F5 non-high: 72 stocks whose first split + 1 falls after the sample stay never treated.
